_README: Frozen shared contract for the post-adapter keypoint representation that BOTH platform adapters must emit (spec docs/semaphore-translator-spec.md sections 3.2, 4.1, 4.2). This is the cross-platform spine: the per-platform adapter is the ONLY code that may touch native skeleton schemas, coordinate origins, or the camera mirror; everything downstream (feature extraction, classification, decode) consumes this exact representation and must be logically identical across iOS and Android. Human-readable spec + per-platform mapping guidance + verification: shared/ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md. Issue #13 (Epic 2).

value_notes.x: normalized to [0,1]; increases toward the SIGNER'S RIGHT (+x = signer's right)
value_notes.y: normalized to [0,1]; increases UP (y-up). The screen/image y-down axis is negated ONCE, in the adapter.
value_notes.confidence: per-keypoint visibility in [0,1], passed through unmodified from the native pose estimator

keypoints.left_right_semantics: left_* is the signer's ANATOMICAL LEFT arm; right_* is the signer's ANATOMICAL RIGHT arm. Because +x points to the signer's right, a signer facing the camera with arms relaxed has right_shoulder.x > left_shoulder.x. Getting native left/right correct under front-camera mirroring is the adapter's single most error-prone job; see ADAPTER-CONTRACT.md.

coordinate_frame.matches: the frozen angle convention in spec 4.2 (angle = atan2(wrist.y - shoulder.y, wrist.x - shoulder.x), measured CCW from +x) and the position model in semaphore_alphabet.json._position_model; position ids 0..7 sit at -90, -45, 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, -135 degrees
transforms_owned_by_adapter: y-flip: negate image y so the frame is y-up (once, at ingest)
horizontal mirror: undo the front-camera mirror so coordinates are in the signer's perspective (+x = signer's right)
coordinate_frame.transforms_rule: Both flips happen EXACTLY ONCE, in the per-platform adapter, and NOWHERE else. Cross-platform divergence almost always traces to one platform's adapter getting one of these two flips wrong -- which the parity harness (#14) and native fixtures (Epic 3) exist to catch.

confidence_gate.rule: An arm is indeterminate if its shoulder OR wrist confidence is below MIN_KEYPOINT_CONFIDENCE (spec 4.3). The adapter only PASSES confidence through; the floor is applied downstream in feature extraction, identically on both platforms. Confidence on the elbow is carried for completeness but does not gate (only shoulder + wrist define the arm vector).

model_input_order._note: INPUT-side analogue of semaphore_alphabet.json.label_order (the OUTPUT class order). Pins the flatten order of the trained classifier's fixed-length input vector (spec 5.3) so both the Core ML and LiteRT exports AND both platform adapters index identically. A label-index or preprocessing/order mismatch between the two converted models is the single most common cross-platform ML bug (spec 5.3 note); this freezes the input half of that contract.
model_input_order.confidence_excluded: Confidence is NOT part of the model input (12 floats = 6 keypoints x {x,y}), matching spec 5.3 ('12 values: x,y per point'). Confidence gates indeterminacy upstream of the model. Revisit only if a future model is given confidence as input (spec 9-D, open).

adapter_must_not: compute arm angles or quantize to position ids (that is feature extraction / classification, spec 4.2-4.3)
look up characters or run the numeric-mode state machine (spec 4.5)
apply temporal smoothing or commit timing (spec 4.4, Epic 4)
apply the mirror or the y-flip more than once, or anywhere downstream of the adapter
